conclusions: Recommend gftt_pyramid, 200 features, warmup10, td0, forward/back LK + RANSAC, cv1, A76 affinity within tested scope.
Pyramid n200 completed all three V2 sequences twice with zero restart requests and exactly repeated trajectories.
Compared with GFTT, CPU time improves about 8-12% and P95 latency about 8-14%; easy ATE is ~4.4 cm worse.
FAST hybrid difficult fails at 16.65 m with two restart requests; not recommended as the general ARM default.
GFTT medium ~1.088 m repeats; difficult changes from 0.488 m to 13.572 m with one restart request. Do not hide failure by averaging.
Pyramid n150 fails easy/difficult; n120 has small CPU savings and worse ATE. Retain n200.
RSS is process-level and not consistently lower; this is not a low-memory claim.
limitations: Only three EuRoC V2 mono sequences on one ARM device; two repetitions for GFTT/pyramid200, single screening for FAST/reduced-count configurations.
No claim of statistical significance or universal accuracy; initialization/solver wall-time and thermal/scheduling can affect trajectories.
Temporal endpoint span is not gap-free coverage. ATE must be read together with output counts, max gaps, restart entries and common timestamp sets.
No production default or current user mono configuration was overwritten; standalone opt-in profile uses this device CPU IDs and EuRoC calibration.
New hardware-acceleration, backend, noise or threshold searches were not performed.
